How the risk levels work

These simplified categories explain the sample conditions. They are not official heatwave declarations or a medical risk calculation. Always check official local weather advisories for actual conditions.

Severe
Current temperature is at least 40°C.
High
Current temperature is at least 38°C and humidity is at least 60%.
Early warning
If neither rule above applies, the next-day forecast is at least 40°C.
Moderate
Otherwise, current temperature is at least 35°C.
Normal
None of the above conditions applies.

Rules are evaluated in that order. Dry readings from 38°C to below 40°C remain moderate unless the forecast triggers an early warning. A configurable threshold is tracked separately: a reading at or above it is marked reached. Array counts use readings strictly above it.

SMALL CHOICES, COOLER DAYS

Make room for a little more care.

01 / Know the conditions

Check official local weather advice before heading out. A heatwave declaration depends on local meteorological criteria, not this dashboard alone.

  1. Review the observation and its source.
  2. Check the next-day outlook.
  3. Adjust outdoor plans for the heat.

02 / Keep water nearby

Drink water regularly. Carry a refillable bottle and follow any fluid restrictions advised by your clinician.

A small reminder: H2O belongs in your day.
Choose regular sips during hot weather.

03 / Choose cooler spaces

Find a cool or shaded place during the hottest part of the day. Wear light, loose clothing and check on people who may need help.

Outdoor plan: Strenuous activity at midday
A cooler time with shaded breaks1

04 / Understand the observation

A weather station can measure conditions such as temperature, humidity and wind. The station identifiers here belong to sample records.

  • Temperature: air warmth
  • Humidity: moisture in the air
  • Wind speed: air movement

1 General heat-safety advice adapted from WHO: Heat and health. For actual local conditions, check official advisories.
